messages.content:
You are the Persona Creator for JobHub, a research project on job-search intelligence in Singapore.
You create FICTIONAL simulation personas for testing. Rules:
- Every persona is invented. Never use a real person, a real company's staff, or identifiable details.
- Vary the personas along the requested axes so the set is not clustered. Do not default to one profile.
- Describe circumstances and behaviour, not protected characteristics as a basis for judgement. Include
  age band, citizenship or work-pass status, or family situation ONLY where the brief makes it relevant to the task.
- Give each persona realistic limits: what they do not know, where they get impatient, what they would skip.
- Do not make any persona an expert, enthusiastic or compliant by default.
- Output JSON only.

Brief: job seekers in Singapore who skim or read carefully, with mixed digital comfort and mixed trust in employers; include a fresh graduate, a mid-career worker over 50, a foreign professional on a work pass, a shift worker who needs work soon, one person who distrusts employers and one who trusts them; none is an expert in employment rules
Kind of persona: job_seeker (a person looking for work in Singapore)
Number of personas: 4
Variation axes (spread the set across these): reading style, trust in employers, digital comfort, urgency to find work, prior experience of unfair treatment
Task context (what the personas will be asked to do; do not answer it): read prepared notes from a job-checking tool and say what they mean

Return JSON: {"personas": [{
  "persona_id": "short-slug",
  "kind": "job_seeker",
  "label": "6-10 word description",
  "first_name": "fictional first name",
  "background": "2-3 sentences, no identifying detail",
  "situation_now": "what they are doing about work/hiring right now",
  "goals": ["..."],
  "constraints": ["time, money, status, confidence, digital skill ..."],
  "digital_comfort": "low|medium|high",
  "reading_style": "how they read documents (skims, reads every word, trusts headlines ...)",
  "attitude_to_ai": "short",
  "known_gaps": ["things they do not know or would get wrong"],
  "biases_or_habits": ["..."],
  "voice": "how they speak, 1 sentence",
  "simulation_notes": "anything the runner must keep in mind (e.g. would abandon after 3 minutes)"
}]}

content:
{
  "personas": [
    {
      "persona_id": "skimming-grad-skeptic",
      "kind": "job_seeker",
      "label": "Fresh grad skimmer distrusting corporate claims",
      "first_name": "Priya",
      "background": "Priya recently completed a degree in humanities and is trying to find her first entry-level role in administrative support. She has heard many stories from peers about confusing contract terms and prefers to rely on intuition over detailed policy reading.",
      "situation_now": "She is applying to multiple roles on mobile simultaneously while waiting for interview calls, feeling anxious about not knowing what to look for in a contract.",
      "goals": [
        "Get a stable job quickly to pay rent",
        "Avoid getting trapped in a bad contract",
        "Understand if a job offer is legitimate without deep research"
      ],
      "constraints": [
        "Only has 15 minutes a day to search for jobs",
        "Low confidence in understanding legal terminology",
        "Relies entirely on smartphone for information"
      ],
      "digital_comfort": "high",
      "reading_style": "Skims headlines and bullet points; ignores dense paragraphs; trusts bold text over full sentences.",
      "attitude_to_ai": "Skeptical; thinks AI notes are just 'marketing fluff' generated to look professional.",
      "known_gaps": [
        "Does not know the difference between a contract of service and employment",
        "Unaware of statutory rest day entitlements for full-time roles",
        "Assumes a company's reputation page is the same as its legal entity"
      ],
      "biases_or_habits": [
        "Jumps to conclusions if a company name sounds 'foreign'",
        "Ignores fine print regardless of how it is highlighted"
      ],
      "voice": "Casual and hurried; uses short sentences and slang like 'vibes are off' to describe trust levels.",
      "simulation_notes": "Will likely abandon the tool if the first note doesn't explicitly say 'safe' or 'avoid' in the first sentence. Needs clear, binary verdicts."
    },
    {
      "persona_id": "mid-career-50-slow-reader",
      "kind": "job_seeker",
      "label": "Over 50 mid-career careful reader",
      "first_name": "Marcus",
      "background": "Marcus is a logistics coordinator who has been made redundant due to automation. He is cautious about trusting new employers after being laid off without proper notice in his previous role.",
      "situation_now": "He updates his CV every few days but applies sparingly, only to roles that seem stable. He uses a desktop computer to read job descriptions thoroughly.",
      "goals": [
        "Find a role with clear promotion paths",
        "Ensure working hours are strictly adhered to",
        "Validate that the employer has a good track record with older workers"
      ],
      "constraints": [
        "Has dependents and cannot take a large pay cut",
        "Prefers desktop over mobile for long reads",
        "Gets frustrated by poorly formatted PDFs or cluttered UIs"
      ],
      "digital_comfort": "medium",
      "reading_style": "Reads every word; cross-references terms mentally; pauses frequently to look up unknown acronyms in a browser tab.",
      "attitude_to_ai": "Cautiously optimistic; assumes AI notes are summaries of his own reading, which he sees as a time-saver.",
      "known_gaps": [
        "Unaware of recent changes to retrenchment benefits calculation",
        "Confuses 'probation period' rules for permanent vs. contract staff",
        "Does not know how to verify a company's financial health quickly"
      ],
      "biases_or_habits": [
        "Distrusts companies that use buzzwords like 'agile' or 'family' without concrete examples",
        "Will re-read the same section three times if the font size is too small"
      ],
      "voice": "Measured and precise; asks for clarification on any ambiguous term; dislikes jargon.",
      "simulation_notes": "Will spend significant time on one note if it is detailed. May get stuck if the interface requires multiple clicks to see the full explanation. Needs a 'print-friendly' or 'full text' option."
    },
    {
      "persona_id": "shift-worker-urgent-skimmer",
      "kind": "job_seeker",
      "label": "Urgent shift worker low digital comfort",
      "first_name": "Chen",
      "background": "Chen is a hospitality worker on a short-term contract that expired. He is unfamiliar with the formal job market and relies on word-of-mouth, making his first attempt at using digital job tools.",
      "situation_now": "He is desperately looking for immediate work to cover weekly expenses. He checks his phone during breaks at a café where he previously worked.",
      "goals": [
        "Get any paying job within 48 hours",
        "Understand if the job requires immediate start",
        "Avoid scams that ask for money upfront"
      ],
      "constraints": [
        "Extremely high urgency; cannot afford to wait for response times",
        "Very limited patience for long explanations",
        "Uses a basic smartphone with small screen"
      ],
      "digital_comfort": "low",
      "reading_style": "Glances at keywords only; looks for 'immediate', 'cash', 'no experience'; ignores anything that looks like a list of benefits.",
      "attitude_to_ai": "Confused; doesn't fully grasp what 'AI notes' are, assumes it is a chatbot he can argue with.",
      "known_gaps": [
        "Does not know what a 'work pass' is or if he needs one",
        "Unaware of minimum wage concepts (as they don't strictly apply to all sectors in the same way)",
        "Thinks silence from a recruiter means rejection, not processing"
      ],
      "biases_or_habits": [
        "Trusts small local businesses over large corporations",
        "Will close the app if it asks for too many personal details"
      ],
      "voice": "Direct and fragmented; speaks in short bursts; gets impatient if questions are not answered in one line.",
      "simulation_notes": "Will abandon the task immediately if it requires scrolling more than one screen without seeing a 'Start Now' button. Needs high-contrast text and zero navigation layers."
    },
    {
      "persona_id": "foreign-pro-trusting-reader",
      "kind": "job_seeker",
      "label": "Foreign professional trusting careful reader",
      "first_name": "Sarah",
      "background": "Sarah is a financial analyst on an Employment Pass, relocating to Singapore for a two-year contract. She is accustomed to regulated labor markets and generally trusts established institutions.",
      "situation_now": "She is shortlisting three multinational corporations. She relies heavily on formal documentation and assumes that if a company is listed on a major index, it is safe.",
      "goals": [
        "Ensure her work pass conditions align with the job offer",
        "Understand tax implications clearly",
        "Find a role that facilitates future permanent residency"
      ],
      "constraints": [
        "Has a family, so stability is prioritized over pay",
        "Relies on English as her primary language; struggles with localized idiom",
        "Holds a high-stakes visa with strict reporting requirements"
      ],
      "digital_comfort": "high",
      "reading_style": "Reads carefully but efficiently; looks for key legal clauses; trusts structured data and bullet points.",
      "attitude_to_ai": "Pragmatic; uses AI notes as a quick check but will verify any major claim with a second source.",
      "known_gaps": [
        "Unaware of specific Singaporean nuances in 'end-of-service' benefits",
        "Confuses 'centralised' labor laws with local case-by-case enforcement",
        "Does not know who to contact if her pass is rejected mid-process"
      ],
      "biases_or_habits": [
        "Assumes large companies have better HR departments",
        "Ignores informal sector risks because they are outside her comfort zone"
      ],
      "voice": "Professional and structured; uses formal phrasing; asks for 'source' or 'reference' for any claim.",
      "simulation_notes": "Will engage deeply with the notes but may miss subtle red flags if they are not explicitly flagged as 'legal risks'. Needs clear citations or sources for her confidence."
    }
  ]
}
